title: All life is yoga
hookLine: an inner command, a boat to Pondicherry, and yoga in the kitchen
carry: all life is yoga, so offer what you do

cards: Calcutta, early in 1910. Aurobindo has been out of jail less than a year, and word comes that the police mean to arrest him again.
He says he heard an inner command, adesh, he called it: go to Chandernagore, a French town up the river. Within minutes, the story goes, he was on a boat.
A few weeks later he sailed south to Pondicherry, another French town, and stayed there the rest of his life. The fiery political leader was gone. So did he go off to sit in a cave?

teach.b: No. In Pondicherry he wrote the book that sets out his way, The Synthesis of Yoga, and near its start stand four words: all life is yoga. Not some of life.
All of it: the cooking, the job, the argument, the walk home. Behind it stands one of the Gita's great teachings.

teach.h: WHATEVER YOU DO, DO IT AS AN OFFERING.
teach.b: Krishna tells Arjuna: whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you offer or give, do it as an offering to me. That's karma yoga, the yoga of work: action given to God.

teach.h: WORK, LOVE, KNOWLEDGE: GATHERED INTO ONE.
teach.b: The Gita also speaks of bhakti, the yoga of love, and jnana, the yoga of knowledge. Aurobindo doesn't make anyone choose. He gathers all three into one practice and calls it integral yoga.
Then he goes a step further. Some paths, he says, aim to rise out of the world. His aim is for the divine to come down into it and change it: body, mind, ordinary life.
Yesterday's cell sits underneath this. If Vasudeva can stand in prison walls, no chore is too low to be part of the yoga. You can see the teaching in an ordinary Hindu kitchen.

teach.h: FOOD OFFERED FIRST, THEN EATEN AS PRASAD.
teach.b: In many homes, food is cooked for God and offered at the shrine first, as bhog or naivedya, and only then eaten as prasad, blessed food. Other Hindu teachers read life's final goal differently.

teach.h: DON'T LEAVE. BRING IT ALL IN.
teach.b: Aurobindo's word to that long conversation was simple: don't leave. Bring it all in.

how: In many Hindu homes food is offered at the shrine before it is eaten as prasad, and those who follow Sri Aurobindo's integral yoga try to offer their daily work, relationships and study in the same spirit; at the Pondicherry ashram, everyday work is treated as part of the practice.

o: a scholar who ranked work above love and knowledge
a hermit who never wrote a single book
the teacher of integral yoga: all life is yoga

p: food offered to God, then shared

s: Aurobindo taught that real yoga means leaving ordinary life behind
he wrote that all life is yoga, and aimed for the divine to change the world, not escape it.
his way gathers the yogas of work, love and knowledge into one
that's the synthesis in The Synthesis of Yoga; he calls it integral yoga.
Aurobindo moved to Pondicherry to hide from the world in a cave
he followed what he called an inner command, and taught that all life, chores included, is yoga.

games.q: it's your turn to cook for the family. you've got Krishna's line and Aurobindo's four words in your head. how do you cook?
o: fast, so you can get back to your 'real' spiritual practice.
as an offering: the cooking is part of the yoga.
not at all; spiritual people shouldn't waste time on chores.
games.why: 'whatever you do, do it as an offering', says Krishna; all life is yoga, says Aurobindo. many Hindu homes offer the food at the shrine before it's eaten as prasad.

practice: Bring to mind the next ordinary thing you'll do after this, a meal, a chore, a message to answer, and see yourself doing it slowly, step by step. Then do what the Gita asks, and hold it out as an offering before you begin.

If you pray, offer it in your own words, to Krishna or to the one you pray to, the way food is set before the home shrine before anyone eats; if you don't, decide to give it the care you'd give a gift.

wordCard.voice: Aurobindo. The teacher of integral yoga, who wrote that all life is yoga, and gathered work, love and knowledge into one way.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: purna yoga, 'full' or 'complete' yoga, a name used for Aurobindo's integral yoga.

carryVoice: Your line: all life is yoga, so offer what you do. Tomorrow, an old story you already know, told his way. See you then.
